thread:
Carla (support): FYI we started getting a cluster of customer reports ~7m ago that hosted inference calls are returning 502/504. Error rate spiking ~8%. Customers: two mid-market customers and a couple of PLG apps. Full timeline below. :rotating_light:
Alice (infra): thanks — any common denominator (route, model, region)?
Carla (support): all hitting /v1/generate (text completion). Region: us-west1. Fast failure pattern, looks like gateway/proxy errors, not model OOMs.
Jae (oncall): I see increased 502s in the gateway from the canary pool for routing-service-v2. Canary tag started at 08:12 UTC. Are you rolling anything?
DeployBot: deploy orch/routing-service:v2.3.1 -> canary (18% traffic) started by @alice at 08:12:03 UTC
Alice (infra): yep that canary. It includes a small proxy change: we now normalize/strip the X-Client-Source header and enforce header-only auth passthrough when the flag enforce-forwarded-headers=true. It was supposed to be opt-in for canary only.
Marta (sre): quick sanity: are upstream auth tokens being forwarded correctly? If auth fails we'd see 401s usually, 502 suggests upstream closing connection or a proxy misroute.
Sam I.: I pulled logs from proxy-canary instances, seeing repeated 502 with message: "upstream connection reset before headers" and occasional 504s. No 401s in those traces.
Carla (support): customers sent curl repros, they see 502 consistently. Provided example: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Alice (infra): reproduce locally hitting canary gateway shows same. I suspect the header normalization is causing the proxy to drop some required internal header (x-route-tag) so requests are sent to the wrong backend pool and then 502. The new code path also fast-closes on missing routing hints.
Jae (oncall): can we toggle the canary flag off quickly? Which flag exactly?
Alice (infra): flag name is enforce-forwarded-headers and it was flipped in the rollout config. I can flip it off for the entire canary pool using the rollout API: 
```
# remove enforcement for canary
curl -X POST "https://internal-control/api/rollout/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL" -d '{"flag":"enforce-forwarded-headers","scope":"canary","value":false}'
```
Marta (sre): while Alice runs that, add temporary routing fallback to stable for affected routes: set route-fallback=stable for /v1/generate in us-west1. That will keep traffic flowing while we confirm. Also open a coordinated rollback ticket if that toggle doesn't reduce errors in 3m.
Alice (infra): toggle sent. Response: 200 OK. Propagating...
Sam I.: metrics showing error rate dropping on canary pool within ~90s — from 8% -> 0.7% — but still some bursts.
Carla (support): passing this to customers: "We identified a canary proxy change and temporarily disabled the enforcement flag while we investigate. You may see intermittent 502/504s cleared." Customers acknowledged.
Jae (oncall): please capture a full heap/profile and tcpdump on one canary instance in case there was an early crash/close bug. Command: 
```
kubectl exec -n canary svc/proxy-canary-0 -- tcpdump -w /tmp/cap.pcap -s 0 'host auth.svc.internal'
```
Alice (infra): starting tcpdump and a pprof snapshot.
Marta (sre): also add a K/V cache check — the new proxy path touches route-lookup cache TTL change. If the cache returns empty it triggers fallback to an internal sidecar which we observed can return 502 on load. Run this: 
```
redis-cli -h route-cache.us-west1 get route:/v1/generate
```
Sam I.: route cache shows empty for a subset of keys around the canary start time. Looks like the patch changed the cache key normalization (stripping client headers changed key).
Alice (infra): confirmed — cache misses explain the misrouted calls. The enforcement path normalized header order which altered the hash key. So requests were routed to a pool that doesn't have the model shard -> upstream rejected -> 502.
Jae (oncall): action items: 1) keep flag disabled for canary and monitor for 30m, 2) schedule immediate rollback of orch/routing-service:v2.3.1 if residual error >0.5% for 30m, 3) full postmortem with PR diff and test gap.
Carla (support): I'll keep affected customer threads updated and waive quota overage alerts for them while we triage. Also creating a billing ticket in case of incorrect metering during failures.
DeployBot: rollback orch/routing-service -> stable at request of @jae queued.
Alice (infra): starting canary rollback now; kubectl rollout undo on the canary replicaset and draining canary pods.
Sam I.: rollback complete across canary nodes, gateway errors in us-west1 dropped back to baseline. No additional billing anomalies flagged so far.
Marta (sre): please add an automated integration test that validates route cache key stability when header normalization features are toggled. Put it in canary gating.
Alice (infra): agreed, opening PR with test and adding a gate to rollout pipeline.
Carla (support): customers updated — all good now, closing incident once postmortem draft is up. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
